source.title: rSDNet: Unified Robust Neural Learning against Label Noise and Adversarial Attacks

record.tranche_reason: Tests performance under uniform label corruption using a different robust-learning objective and benchmark losses; it does not apply fully random labels.
record.gate_note: The study varies uniform label-noise rates from 0.1 to 0.5 and reports cross-validated accuracy on clean folds. It does not report training error on corrupted training folds. Mentions of memorization and dropout in the Introduction cite prior work and are not study results.
record.test_reason: The study cites random-label memorization as motivation for robust losses, but measures held-out accuracy and its stabilization over epochs. It never measures fitting corrupted training labels. Its mitigation results therefore do not test the memorization behavior specified by these versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that appropriately tuned rSDNet preserves competitive clean-data accuracy while improving resistance to label noise and adversarial perturbations. They restrict their empirical conclusions to relatively simple image classifiers and leave larger architectures and comprehensive convergence analysis for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Uses S-divergence loss with Adam, compared with the original studies' standard training settings; experiments introduce uniform label noise rather than completely random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with dataset, corruption rate and rSDNet tuning parameters (β, λ).

fits_no_version.finding: CCE clean-fold accuracy falls from clean training to 50% label corruption: MNIST 0.9816 to 0.5201, Fashion-MNIST 0.8891 to 0.6205, and CIFAR-10 0.6782 to 0.3004. Robust-loss performance depends on the dataset and loss parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Held-out classification accuracy degrades under increasing uniform incorrect-label replacement, and suitable robust losses can reduce that degradation. These measurements do not establish memorization of corrupted training labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix B reports slower and less stable test-accuracy convergence for CCE and TCCE under 20% and 40% label noise, while rSDNet retains comparatively fast stabilization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Label noise affects the trajectory of held-out accuracy differently across training objectives; this does not measure the time required to fit random labels.

record.problems: No training accuracy is reported for corrupted-label experiments. Results use relatively simple MLP and CNN image classifiers, and the authors say larger modern architectures remain future work. Numerical results are cross-validated accuracies without reported uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows retained: the reported corrupted-label accuracies are test/validation-fold accuracies, without a measure of training-set fit, so they cannot establish the joint behavior specified by V4. Tables 2–4 report accuracies at corruption rates 0.1–0.5; Appendix B Figures 5–6 show convergence curves but provide no numerical training-time values.

untested.parts: No completely random labeling, corrupted-label training error, or corresponding chance-level test-error experiment.
No time-to-fit comparison for true versus random labels. Appendix B measures stabilization of test accuracy, which cannot establish convergence to a fit of noisy training labels.
No fitting experiments with shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Clean-fold accuracy is measured through 50% incorrect-label replacement, but perfect training fit and the joint memorization/generalization trajectory toward completely random labels are untested.
No controlled addition or removal of weight decay, dropout, or augmentation testing random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
No separate learning trajectories for correctly labeled and mislabeled training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's T2 classification and V4 tested status. The omitted tables and convergence figures are already declared in rows_left_out. Corruption replaces labels with incorrect classes; for these ten-class datasets, completely uniform random labels correspond to a replacement rate of 0.9, beyond the tested maximum of 0.5.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment uses completely random labels or reports training error and chance-level test error under random labels.
Appendix B compares convergence behavior under clean, 20% and 40% label noise, but does not test fitting random labels, quantify training time, or report a constant-factor comparison.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel or Gaussian-noise input experiment.

The study tests uniform label corruption at rates 0.1–0.5 and reports clean-fold accuracy, but does not report training-set fit, test error through 100% corruption, or whether degradation is steadily monotonic for each model across the full range.
No experiment removes weight decay, dropout or augmentation, or tests their effects on random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
No training-time analysis of whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
